comment: Model catalogue. Every entry here is pinned: the file name, byte size and SHA-256 were read
from the mudler/parakeet-cpp-gguf file listing, where the LFS oid is the SHA-256 of the blob.
ModelInstaller checks every download against these digests and moves nothing into place that
does not match.
The f16 digest was independently corroborated: a copy installed and used for three hours of
audio hashed to the same value the repository publishes.
An entry added later with "sha256": null still works, but it downloads unverified and both
the CLI and the UI say so on its face. See docs/MODELS.md before adding one.
Sizes are exact and are compared to the downloaded byte count, so a rounded value is a bug.
An entry is one file or several. One file names it inline — "fileName", "url", "sizeBytes",
"sha256" — and lands in the store root, which is every entry below. Several go in a "files"
array of those same four keys, and then "directory" is required: the ONNX translation route
ships config.json and vocab.json, and no single entry can own those names in a shared folder.
An entry carrying both shapes is refused rather than guessed at. Pins are per file, so an entry
is verified only when every one of its files is — eight of nine is unverified.
A multi-file entry installs all or nothing: the installer assembles it in a <directory>.part
staging folder and renames that into place once every file has been sized and hashed, so an
interrupted download is never something an engine can be handed. Resume is per file.
Weights are CC BY 4.0 (NVIDIA). Redistribution is permitted and the notice obligations are in
Licensing/Attribution.cs — they are not satisfied by attribution alone.
An entry may carry "task": "transcription" (the default when absent), "diarisation" or
"translation". A non-transcription entry installs through the same URL, size and digest checks
and is never offered as an ASR model: not by `transcribe`, not as the recommended entry, not to
the window's Load button. Each discriminator shipped before the entry it guards, so no build can
carry an entry whose task word it does not know.
There is one diarisation entry now. It is NOT CC BY 4.0 — it is the NVIDIA Open Model License, whose §3.1 wants a
verbatim notice and a copy of the agreement rather than CC BY's seven elements. The Agreement was
read in full at NVIDIA's own URL on 2026-08-19 and permits redistribution; docs/LICENSING.md
records what it obliges and where the two licences differ. Its URL is pinned to a revision rather
than to main, because it belongs to a single-maintainer third party rather than to NVIDIA.
There is one translation entry, the first multi-file one: nine files in a directory of its own,
each with its own size and SHA-256. The nine digests are the ones the gate run itself recorded
for the artefact it scored, re-hashed off disk on 2026-08-20 and matching byte for byte.
**It is verified, and the nine digests are attested twice over.** They were first taken off the
bytes the gate run scored and re-hashed from disk; the files were then published to Hugging Face
on 2026-08-20, and every one of the nine LFS oids the repository publishes — an LFS oid IS the
file's SHA-256 — matched the scored digest. That is stronger than any other entry here, which
rest on the listing alone. The upload forces all nine onto LFS including the four under a
kilobyte: an ordinary git blob has a git SHA-1 and publishes no SHA-256, and an entry is as
verified as its least-checked member.
The URLs pin a COMMIT SHA rather than main, the way the diarisation entry does and for the same
reason: a URL and a digest are pinned together here, so a URL that can serve different bytes
later breaks every installed copy with a digest mismatch as the only symptom.
Apache-2.0, and the third licence shape in Attributions: section 4(a) wants a copy of the licence
rather than a link, so licences/Apache-License-2.0.txt ships. docs/LICENSING.md records what is
still open on it.
See docs/PHASES.md.

models.notes: The smallest step down from f16, and measured against human transcripts: 10.23% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of accented English earnings calls (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md) — no measurable cost on that corpus. Divergence from f16 is 0.42% of tokens over 2 h 55 m; that is which words differ, not how many are wrong. One English corpus of one genre, scored with this project's own normaliser, is the whole of the evidence: it is enough to say this entry is not the silent collapse the analogous ONNX INT8 export was, and not enough to say more. Saves about 500 MB of download and some CPU decode time.

Default choice, and the reference for accuracy: 10.21% word error rate against verbatim human transcripts of eleven hours of accented English earnings calls, 13.40% against non-verbatim ones (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md; this project's own normaliser, so not comparable to a published figure). It is the default because it was the one entry whose quality was not an open question when the choice was made; every quantisation in the catalogue has since scored within 0.08 points of it on that corpus, and whether one of them should replace it as the default is an open product decision. The cost is a 1.34 GiB download and a slower CPU decode than q8_0.

10.17% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of human-transcribed accented English (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md) — no measurable cost on that one corpus, which is the whole of the evidence.

10.17% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of human-transcribed accented English (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md) — no measurable cost on that one corpus, which is the whole of the evidence.

Smallest, and the one most likely to fail silently — which it did not: 10.15% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of human-transcribed accented English (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md), while differing from f16 on 2.69% of tokens over 2 h 55 m — differently right and differently wrong, not more wrong. One English corpus of one genre is the whole of the evidence.

Says who spoke when; it does not transcribe. Measured on AMI test, 16 meetings, 9.06 h: DER 16.33% at collar 0 with overlap scored and 13.60% at this project's headline collar of 0.25, against the pyannote only_words references — post-processing fixed on the 18 development meetings and applied unchanged, test scored once (docs/PHASES.md). Two limits belong on its face. It tells apart at most FOUR speakers, architecturally: a fifth voice is merged into one of the four, no measurement here prices what that costs, and NVIDIA's own figures for five-plus speakers in this configuration are 34.81% and 38.90% against about 15% below the cap. And it buffers 30.4 s, so it trails the audio by half a minute — fine for a file, not a live-captioning latency. The size is the fp32 graph: the `quantized` tag on the Hub is wrong, and 473 of the 474 MB are float32 weights. Languages are unlisted because it models voices rather than words; it was trained on English meeting corpora and nothing here measures it on anything else.

models.displayName: OPUS-MT Bible-Big multilingual to English - ONNX fp32
models.notes: Rewrites a finished transcript in English; it does not transcribe and it reads no audio. Many-to-one: it is told the target and never the source, so nothing has to detect what was spoken. Measured on the desktop's CPU on 2026-08-20 against FLEURS test in full, 8,149 sentences in 24 languages, beam-6, batch 1, chrF++ at nrefs:1|case:mixed|eff:yes|nc:6|nw:2|space:no|version:2.6.0: 44.26 (Slovak) to 68.52 (Portuguese), clearing the per-language source-copy floor by +28.15 to +60.53, with zero degenerate collapses. Against the gate's bar of 45 minus that floor, 23 of the 24 pass and SLOVAK FAILS BY 0.74 — it is the one language this entry is known not to meet the project's own bar in. The gate as a whole is NOT passed: its second criterion is a human adequacy check that nobody has performed (docs/PHASES.md, docs/UNPROVEN.md). The 25 language tags are list membership rather than a quality claim — the checkpoint's own card disclaims its coverage list in as many words, English is a byte-identical passthrough rather than a translation, and 23 of the 25 have never had audio through this pipeline at all. CPU only, and that is priced rather than assumed: CUDA was measured on 2026-08-20 at 1.2-1.5x for this model's fp32 output against 22x for the diariser, and one ONNX Runtime native serves both. Translation carries no word timings, so -f vtt-words is refused rather than written against times that no longer belong to the words. int8 (345.9 MiB) and fp16 (686.4 MiB) both exist in the export and neither ships: int8 was dropped on speed and a silent CUDA collapse without its quality ever being scored, and fp16 does not load at all. Nine files, 1.34 GiB, installed all or nothing.

deferredComment: Files in the same repository whose digests are recorded so a later version does not have to
re-derive them. They are NOT catalogue entries and this build cannot install or select them.
The reason they are not is licensing, not caution about quality. Every entry in "models"
carries a licence and an attribution id that resolves against Attribution.ById, because the
app shows that notice and CC BY is not satisfied by attribution alone. These two families are
not parakeet-tdt: Nemotron models commonly ship under the NVIDIA Open Model License rather
than CC BY 4.0, and realtime_eou has no stated provenance in the file listing at all. Naming
a licence for either would be inventing one, and it would put a false notice in front of a
So what is recorded is only what was read from the listing: name, exact size, SHA-256. To
promote one, establish the licence, register the attribution, and move it into "models".
